source_caption:
🎬 The Simple Life of Noah Dearborn (1999)

The Simple Life of Noah Dearborn follows Noah Dearborn, an elderly carpenter living a peaceful and independent life on his small farm in rural Georgia. Known for his remarkable craftsmanship, gentle personality, and strong connection to the land, Noah has spent decades working with his hands and appreciating life’s simplest pleasures. However, his quiet existence is threatened when a powerful businessman becomes determined to acquire his property for a major development project. Refusing to sell the land that holds his memories and life’s work, Noah finds himself facing increasing pressure from people who believe his age and unusual lifestyle make him incapable of managing his own affairs. As the conflict intensifies, a legal effort is made to have him declared mentally incompetent, threatening his freedom and independence. During this difficult time, Noah develops an unexpected friendship with Valerie, a troubled psychologist who gradually becomes fascinated by his wisdom, kindness, and extraordinary outlook on life. Through their conversations and growing connection, Valerie begins questioning her own understanding of happiness, success, and what truly matters. As Noah fights to protect his home and dignity, his quiet determination inspires those around him to reconsider their priorities. Combining heartfelt performances, emotional storytelling, and meaningful life lessons, The Simple Life of Noah Dearborn explores independence, friendship, compassion, resilience, aging, and the beauty of finding happiness in life’s simplest moments.

🎭 Genre: Drama • Family

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 27m • TV-PG

🎥 Director: Gregg Champion

✍️ Writers: Sterling Anderson & John Gray

source_details.synopsis: The Simple Life of Noah Dearborn, is a 1999 American television film aired on May 9, 1999 on CBS. It stars Sidney Poitier as the eponymous rural Georgia skilled carpenter, who lives alone without electricity and seems frozen in time. George Newbern played a developer trying to force Dearborn off his land. He tries to enlist the help of his psychologist girlfriend (Mary-Louise Parker), a move which backfires badly. The developer tries to have Dearborn declared mentally incompetent; the effort fails, mostly because of the efforts of the woman, who realizes why Dearborn is held in esteem by his neighbors. For her performance, Dianne Wiest was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding
